item.title: Re: Which SCP-001 Proposal Is The Real One?
item.content:encoded:
I believe that it wouldn't make sense (in my headcanon) for the foundation to have a "first" SCP be SCP-001. An arbitrary number is given to any object that happens to be available for it. Why can't 001 be one of those arbitrary numbers? Order of discovery would be irrelevant.

That being said, I'd consider either A Record, Thirty-Six, The Database, or The Consensus to be the canon SCP-001. I can't decide between those four.

item.title: Re: Which SCP-001 Proposal Is The Real One?
item.content:encoded:
I canon pretty much all SCPs co-existing in the same universe, and -001s are too big to play nice.

Dr. Mann's Proposal is discovered, and anomalies begin to sprout from that tear in reality. At around the same time, Jonathan Ball's Proposal is discovered and begins documenting these anomalies as they are created. Every opening of Ball's Proposal corresponds to an anomaly created from Mann's Proposal. Multiple organizations dedicated to preserving normalcy pop up due to the presence of anomalies within the natural world. Dr. Clef's Proposal, qntm's Proposal, Dr. Bright's Proposal, and Dr Gears' Proposal are all SCP-001s for one of these agencies. Scantron's Proposal IS one of these agencies. Time passess, anomalies are contained, and then the Fifth Occult War and Wrong Proposal happens. After a short dispute, multiple entries are assigned to the 001 spot due to their importance to the component organizations. The Foundation as we know it has been created. Over time, more anomalies are discovered or created. These include Dr. Mackenzie's Proposal, Djoric-Dmatix Proposal, djkaktus's Proposal, and TwistedGears-Kaktus Proposal. Mary Nakayama ascends to godhood through Kate McTiriss's Proposal but is unable to do anything about the anomalies because they…come from another universe or something. (Wasn't that a key part of Mackenzie's Proposal?) SCP-2798 fails, and Kalinin's Proposal occurs. Humanity doesn't leave though, and so Entity Thaumiel gets desperate and reckless. It then makes the dumb decision of modifying the sun. Things didn't go quite as well as expected, but it did cause S. D. Locke's Proposal to happen. And that was that. Of course, none of it mattered because it was all fictional (S Andrew Swann's Proposal).

Oh, and Roget's Proposal probably fits in there somewhere.

item.title: Re: Which SCP-001 Proposal Is The Real One?
item.content:encoded:
Favorite in regards to prose/believability/etc? Probably either Roget's or Scantron's.

Which one is the real SCP-001? In my headcanon, if there really is one, it's probably the one Gears wrote. That said, I believe there's no SCP-001, at least not ones that we read here. In my headcanon, there's no actual SCP-001; all the proposals, are in some parallel universe, canon. My headcanon has always been "everything is canon", because I think SCP reports/tales aren't only a slice of time, but also a slice of space. There's no indication that this SCP exists in a completely different plane of reality as we are. All these overlaps, discrepancies, even alternative timelines where tales occur in which the Foundation does not exist or the Foundation became a cult, are in a way, "canon", because they're all occurring withing different universes.

Heck, we might be the universe where the Foundation exists, only there's nothing to contain.
